title: I've spent the last month building a free crypto market intelligence platform. Would love some honest feedback.
author: Naive-Caregiver-9853

comments.author: QATSAlgo
comments.body: Based on the feature list, I would make one scanner result reproducible: exchange, symbol, data timestamp, score version and a short explanation of the inputs that changed the score. Then let a user save that snapshot and compare it with the later simulation, including fees and spread. That gives people a reason to return beyond a fresh AI number. QATS team here; we build trading tools, but this is feedback on your description rather than a completed site review. Can users currently inspect an old score exactly as it appeared at the time?

replies.author: Naive-Caregiver-9853
replies.body: Thanks, useful feedback. Honest answer: not exactly, not yet. Each score in the scanner shows when it was read, and the AI scores and write-ups are timestamped, but you can't currently pull up a past score as it was displayed. What we do keep is a track record: every four hours the scanner's scores are logged and checked against the market 4 hours, 1 day and 3 days later, relative to the median coin, so you can see whether the score bands actually held up over 30 or 90 days. The safety checker also keeps a coin's last ten checks and shows what changed. A saved, reproducible snapshot (exchange, symbol, data time, score version, the inputs that moved it) that you can later compare with a simulation including fees and spread is a good idea. It's going on the list!

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: crypto spreads on the smaller coins can eat a sim's whole edge, so the fill rule is where I'd poke first. does a simulated buy fill at the last price on the chart or at the ask?
